title: Guarding the Sacred Fire
captions: “This is Siddhashrama,” said Vishvamitra. “Long ago Lord Vishnu, as Vamana, did tapas here. It is my hermitage, and here I will perform my yajna.”
The sages of the hermitage welcomed them with joy. That very day Vishvamitra lit the sacred fire and began the yajna, taking a vow of silence.
“Our teacher will not speak until the yajna is done,” the sages told the princes. “Guard it for six days and six nights.”
Rama and Lakshmana stood guard with their bows ready. Through the long days and dark nights they did not sleep, watching the forest all around.
On the sixth day, the sacred fire blazed up high. Then a great roar filled the sky, and the rakshasas Maricha and Subahu swooped down with their army.
Rama did not wish to take Maricha's life. He sent the Manava astra, and it carried Maricha far away across the sky and dropped him into the distant ocean.
With the fire astra Rama struck down Subahu, and with the wind astra he blew the rest away. The yajna was complete, and the sages praised the brave princes.
story: Vishvamitra led the princes into the peaceful grove. “This is Siddhashrama,” he said. Long ago, Lord Vishnu had done tapas there before he came into the world as Vamana. Now it was Vishvamitra's hermitage, and there he would perform his yajna.

The sages of the hermitage welcomed them with joy. That same day, Vishvamitra lit the sacred fire and began his yajna. He took a vow of silence, which meant he would not speak until the yajna was complete.

The other sages explained the task to the princes: guard the yajna for six days and six nights. Rama and Lakshmana stood ready with their bows. They did not sleep. They watched the forest through the bright days and the long, dark nights.
On the sixth day, the sacred fire blazed up high. Then a great roar filled the sky, and the rakshasas Maricha and Subahu swooped down with their army, ready to spoil the ceremony.

Rama did not wish to take Maricha's life. He used the Manava astra, which carried Maricha far across the sky and dropped him into the distant ocean. With the fire astra Rama struck down Subahu, and with the wind astra he drove the rest away. The yajna was complete, and the sages praised the brave princes.
lesson: Rama and Lakshmana were given one job: to guard the sacred fire. They did it for six days and six nights without sleeping, even when nothing seemed to be happening. When danger finally came, they were ready. In our tradition, Kartavya means doing our duty fully and faithfully, whether the task is exciting or quiet, and whether or not anyone is watching.
lesson_long: Kartavya means duty: the work that is ours to do, done fully and faithfully.

Rama and Lakshmana were given one job, to guard the sacred fire. For six days and six nights they stayed alert, even when nothing seemed to be happening. That is the hardest part of duty: staying careful when everything is quiet. When danger finally came, they were ready.
Our elders teach that duty done well does not need anyone watching. We do it because it is ours to do.
tradition: In the Bhagavad Gita, Lord Krishna teaches that we should do our duty well and not worry too much about the reward. This is called karma yoga, the path of doing good work with a calm heart.

Vamana, who is remembered at Siddhashrama, is the fifth avatar of Lord Vishnu. He came as a small boy and asked King Bali for three steps of land. Then he grew so large that he covered the earth and the sky in just two steps.
words: Vishvamitra's hermitage, a place where tapas brings success
the fifth avatar of Lord Vishnu
doing good work without worrying about the reward
question: What is one job you do at home or at school? How can you do it well, even when no one is watching?
questions: What is one job you do at home or at school? How can you do it well, even when no one is watching?
Why was it hard for the princes to stay alert when nothing was happening?
Rama chose not to take Maricha's life. Why might he have chosen that?
